summary: Hidden conversion-smoothing fee on finalized invoice; hourly smoothing credit not applied after rate-plan conversion
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports an unexpected fee line labeled 'conversion-smoothing' on a finalized March invoice. At the same time hourly smoothing credits that usually offset microburst embed spikes were not applied for three separate bursts on 2026-03-02. The customer believes this is correlated with the org's recent rate-plan conversion performed by billing ops on 2026-03-01.

Impact: Finalized invoice USD 23,412.85 contains a new fee line of USD 412.50 and is missing -USD 375.00 in hourly-smoothing credits that NimbleDocs expected. Net unexpected charge ~USD 37.50. Customer is on enterprise contract and flagged as billing-impacting; they require an explanation and corrective credit.

Environment: prod, us-east; account id: org_009874; invoice id: INV-2026-03-009874; affected API keys: key-prod-ner-01 (masked).

Steps to reproduce / observation steps:
1) Run our standard invoice reconciliation for org_009874 for period 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07.
2) Inspect invoice line items and hourly smoothing ledger for the account in the billing UI and via /internal/billing/ledger API.
3) Observe presence of a one-off fee labeled 'conversion-smoothing' and absence of three expected smoothing credits that correspond to microburst windows (2026-03-02 02:00-02:15, 09:10-09:20, 17:45-17:50 UTC).

Observed behavior: A new fee line 'conversion-smoothing' (rate_type: conversion-fee) appears on finalized invoice. The hourly_smoothing ledger entries for those three microbursts show status 'pending' and were not promoted to 'applied' during finalization. Postback logs show smoothing job attempted, but the postback for those entries was rejected with a 400 error citing unknown rate_tag 'rp_conv_v2'.

Expected behavior: Hourly smoothing credits should have been applied before invoice finalization. No unexplained conversion fee should be billed to the customer; any rate-plan migration artifact should not create a positive fee without customer visibility.

Attachments: invoice PDF attached to ticket, extracted ledger CSV, postback log excerpt (billing-job-2026-03-02.log lines 412-436).

Requested action: Provide root-cause explanation, apply corrective credit if customer is owed one, and confirm fix to mapping so smoothing credits are applied for retroactive/converted rate plans.

investigation_notes: Initial triage: correlate rate-plan conversion deploy (rp-convert-20260301) with smoothing job failure. Observed error in smoothing-postback-service: 400 Bad Request 'unknown rate_tag rp_conv_v2'. Hypothesis: mapping table used by smoothing-postback-service was not updated atomically with rate-plan conversion and smoothing-service still expected pre-migration tags. Checked mapping delta: rp_conv_v2 introduced but smoothing mapping cache not reloaded due to a deploy race (billing-worker restarted mid-deploy). Logs indicate 2 smoothing postbacks for org_009874 were transitioned to 'pending' and later skipped during finalization because the credit reconciliation job treats pending entries with unrecognized rate_tag as non-applicable. Next steps: (1) Confirm mapping commit and exact deploy timestamps, (2) add idempotent cache-reload step in rate-plan conversion flow, (3) backfill smoothing credits for affected windows and regenerate invoice adjustments where appropriate.
resolution: In progress - provisional credit applied (CR-2026-03-752468). Engineering to patch mapping reload in conversion job and run backfill for pending smoothing entries. Final resolution will include an entry in the account ledger and a comment here when invoice adjustment completes.
resolution_notes: Provisional credit posted on 2026-03-11 13:45 UTC. Billing engineering prepared a backfill script (github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1145) to mark pending smoothing entries as applied when mapping is available. Plan: schedule backfill on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC during maintenance window; if backfill succeeds we will generate an invoice credit note and close ticket. Customer requested a short postmortem; assigning follow-up to Billing Eng to produce a one-page action item list.
